facts: Adam Ziegfeld authored the paper titled 'Varieties of Electoral Dominance'.
The article was published in Comparative Politics on October 1, 2022.
Dominant political parties are defined as parties that rule for prolonged periods by winning successive multiparty elections.

The paper observes that 'dominant party' covers a diverse set ranging from parties with unremarkable vote shares in established democracies to those winning massive majorities in free but unfair elections.

The author proposes a three-part typology based on the foundations of electoral dominance: extremely high vote shares, steadfast support from legislative allies, or a favorable translation of votes into seats or office.
The three proposed dominant-party types are internally homogeneous but distinct from one another.
The paper concludes that the puzzles posed by each dominant-party type, and the answers required to address them, differ markedly.
